[bold #D75FFF]◆ EPIC sase-1tz.4.1[/bold #D75FFF]
[dim]  Title: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]Gateway checkpoint fix, notification hygiene, and retention sweep [/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]         [bold #D7AFFF][/dim](items 11-13)[/bold #D7AFFF]
[dim]   Goal: [#D7D7AF][/dim]A busy SQLite WAL checkpoint reports busy instead of erroring, read[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]paths checkpoint passively, and the gateway serves a cached fleet [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]snapshot at once while one rebuild runs in the background. [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]remote-attention keeps one row per request, wait_checks raises one [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]notice per failed root blocker with a one-key expire action, and [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]task-bead triage keeps one notification per bead. Settled triage [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]gate bundles are reaped. Notification payloads over 8 KB move to [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]sidecar files, and broken file references are pruned. file-hooks [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]successes are silent, workspace-rescue dedups, prune nudges have a [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]size floor, agent_state_refresh logs each unchanged verdict once, [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]and no-op claim-ledger rows stop. Tool-run logs, tui.log, proc log [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]locks, registry temp files, and index backups follow stated [/#D7D7AF]
[dim]         [#D7D7AF][/dim]horizons.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim] Counts: [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]13[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] phases[dim][/dim] · [bold #D7AFFF][/dim]3[dim][/bold #D7AFFF] waves[/dim]

[dim] Prompt: [#87AFFF][/dim]prompts/202611/hygiene_gateway_notifications_retention.md[/#87AFFF]

[dim]   Bead: [#87AFFF][/dim]sase-1tz.4.1[/#87AFFF]
[dim]   Page: [#87AFFF][/dim]https://github.com/sase-org/sase--beads/blob/main/pages/sase-1tz/[bold #87AFFF][/#87AFFF]sase-1tz.4.1.md[/bold #87AFFF]
[dim]  1 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Treat SQLite's busy -1 checkpoint result as busy and [/bold #D7AFFF]         [bold black on #87D7FF] small  [/bold black on #87D7FF]
      [bold #D7AFFF]checkpoint passively on read paths[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]wal_busy[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]wal_busy: in sase-core, a busy wal_checkpoint that returns -1 counts [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]reports checkpoint_busy instead of failing u64 conversion. The gateway's[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]post-build hook uses PASSIVE and runs after waiters are woken. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Maintenance keeps TRUNCATE. Move the pin.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  2 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Serve cached fleet snapshots stale-while-revalidate in the [/bold #D7AFFF]   [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]gateway[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]gateway_swr[dim] · [dim][/dim]after wal_busy[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]gateway_swr: an expired cached snapshot is served at once, marked stale,[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]while one background rebuild runs. Index-permit waits are bounded. A [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]cold cache keeps today's bounded wait. Record the relationship on [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]sase-1s5 and move the pin.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  3 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Key remote-attention rows by stable request identity[/bold #D7AFFF]          [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]attention_key[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]attention_key: remote-attention rows key on (origin, request_id). A new [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]revision updates and resurfaces the one row. An identical re-emission [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]writes nothing. A local dismissal still sticks for its revision. Legacy [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]per-revision rows migrate once.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  4 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Add opt-in sidecar storage for oversize notification payloads [bold black on #FFD75F][/bold #D7AFFF] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]in sase-core[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]blob_store[dim] · [dim][/dim]after attention_key[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]blob_store: sase-core stores action_data values and notes over a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]caller-supplied byte limit as content-addressed sidecar files, with a [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]read binding. Compaction garbage-collects unreferenced sidecars and [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]prunes broken files references. Default behavior is unchanged. Move the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pin.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  5 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Resolve sidecar payloads in every reader, then externalize [/bold #D7AFFF]   [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]payloads over 8 KB[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]blob_adopt[dim] · [dim][/dim]after blob_store[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]blob_adopt: the TUI, Telegram, and mobile readers that need full [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]action_data or note text resolve sidecar references. Then the Python [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]store wrapper externalizes payloads over 8 KB by default, and live [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]oversize rows migrate once.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  6 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Raise one wait_checks notice per failed root blocker and [/bold #D7AFFF]     [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]freeze its +1s[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]wait_blocker[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]wait_blocker: terminally blocked waiters group under one notice per root[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]blocker that names every direct and transitive waiter. The notice [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]changes only when its waiter set changes and never +1s otherwise. Legacy[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]per-waiter rows settle once.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  7 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Offer a one-key action that expires a failed blocker's waiters[bold black on #FFD75F][/bold #D7AFFF] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]waiter_expire[dim] · [dim][/dim]after wait_blocker[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]waiter_expire: under blocked_waiters = offer, the root-blocker notice [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]gets a one-key TUI action. It expires every waiter the notice names [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]through the existing user cancel path for a waiting agent, records the [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]blocker as the reason, and settles the notice. Nothing expires waiters [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]automatically.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  8 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Keep one task-triage notification per bead across presentation[bold black on #FFD75F][/bold #D7AFFF] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
      [bold #D7AFFF]changes[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]triage_volume[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]triage_volume: measure which fingerprint inputs churn triage gates. Stop[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]canceling and recreating a pending gate for presentation drift the gate [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]does not render. Recreated gates reuse one notification row per bead. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Remove or keep the quiet-task-beads rule per the decision.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  9 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Settle orphaned triage gates and reap settled gate bundles[/bold #D7AFFF]    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]gate_reconcile[dim] · [dim][/dim]after triage_volume[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]gate_reconcile: a pending automation-owned gate whose notification was [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]dismissed, or whose bead is resolved, is cancelled. A dismissal is not [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]undone by the next pass. Settled task-triage and snooze bundles older [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]than a horizon are reaped. Other gate kinds are only counted.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  10 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Silence success toasts, dedup workspace-rescue, floor prune [/bold #D7AFFF] [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
       [bold #D7AFFF]nudges, and skip no-op claim writes[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]notify_quieting[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]notify_quieting: file-hooks successes become one silent row per hook, [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]and workspace-rescue gets a stable dedup key. Artifact-run prune nudges [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]fire only above a size floor or under disk pressure. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]hold_workspace_claim writes no ledger row when nothing changed.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  11 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Log each unchanged agent_state_refresh verdict once[/bold #D7AFFF]          [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
    [#AF87FF]state_refresh_memo[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]state_refresh_memo: agent_state_refresh persists each run's unresolved [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]verdict with an evidence fingerprint. A pass that sees the same [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]fingerprint skips the warning and the dismissed-bundle lookup. A changed[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]fingerprint re-evaluates and logs once. Stays clear of sase-1s5.3's [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]lookup changes.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  12 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Apply the tool-run log horizon on a schedule, age-rotate [/bold #D7AFFF]    [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
       [bold #D7AFFF]tui.log, and verify digest and run pruning[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]log_horizons[dim] · [dim][/dim]no dependencies[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]log_horizons: an hourly housekeeping chop applies the existing tool-run [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]retention owner, not only under disk pressure, and removes emptied run [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]dirs. tui.log rotates by age as well as size. Verify error-digest [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]pruning and that artifact_run_prune is unblocked on both hosts.[/#D7D7AF]
[dim]  13 [bold #AF87FF][/dim]◆ [bold #D7AFFF][/bold #AF87FF]Fix the proc log-lock and registry temp-file leaks and reap [/bold #D7AFFF] [bold black on #FFD75F] medium [/bold black on #FFD75F]
       [bold #D7AFFF]their backlog[/bold #D7AFFF]
    [#AF87FF]clutter_reapers[dim] · [dim][/dim]after log_horizons[/#AF87FF][/dim]
    [#D7D7AF]clutter_reapers: deleting proc logs also removes their lock files. The [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]name-registry writer sweeps its own stale temp files under its lock. [/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]Owner steps reap both backlogs from the log_horizons chop. Index backups[/#D7D7AF]
    [#D7D7AF]follow the index_backups decision.[/#D7D7AF]
